common.disclaimer: IZVOR is a data preparation tool. The user is responsible for the due diligence statement.

home.title: Timber traceability for EUDR – from the forest to the statement in TRACES
home.subtitle: IZVOR is a tool for sawmills, importers and timber traders. Enter plots and documents once; for every shipment you get a correct GeoJSON, the due diligence statement in TRACES and a package for your buyer.
home.deadlineLarge: Large and medium companies: EUDR applies from 30 Dec 2026.
home.deadlineSmall: Micro and small companies: EUDR applies from 30 Jun 2027.
home.ctaText: Get ready in time – prepare your first shipment in minutes.
steps: Enter suppliers, plots (with harvest period) and documents.
Prepare a shipment: products, quantities and plots – the checklist shows what is missing.
Submit the statement in TRACES and send the buyer a package with the DDS numbers.

features.p: Draw a plot on your phone or import GeoJSON, KML, Shapefile, CSV or Excel. National coordinate systems are converted automatically.
6 decimals, polygons above 4 ha, self-intersections, location within the country and duplicates – you see errors at once, and some are fixed with one click.
Felling permits, decisions, delivery notes and certificates linked to plots. We warn you before a document expires.
Submit the due diligence statement directly to the EU Information System; the reference and verification numbers are filled in automatically.
Country risk per the implementing regulation, and a record of the assessment and mitigation for every shipment.
A link or a PDF with a QR code for the buyer and forwarder, a ZIP archive for inspections and a 5-year audit trail.

audiences.p: Buying from forest owners and forest enterprises? Collect geolocations and permits once and reuse them for every shipment.
Importing from Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia or elsewhere? Keep the statement, risk assessment and evidence in one place.

issues.GEOM_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED: Geometry type {type} is not allowed. Use a point or a polygon.
issues.COORD_OUT_OF_RANGE: Coordinates are out of range (longitude −180 to 180, latitude −90 to 90).
issues.COORD_SWAPPED: Latitude and longitude seem to be swapped. Check the column order.
issues.COORD_LOOKS_PROJECTED: Coordinates are in metres (e.g. D96/TM), not WGS-84 degrees. Choose the right coordinate system when importing.
issues.PRECISION_TOO_LOW: Coordinates have only {found} decimal places; at least {required} are required.
issues.PRECISION_PARTIAL: Some coordinates have only {found} decimal places (trailing zeros may have been lost). At least {required} are recommended.
issues.POLYGON_CLOSED_AUTOMATICALLY: The polygon was not closed, so we closed it automatically. Check its shape on the map.
issues.POLYGON_TOO_FEW_POINTS: The polygon has too few points (at least 3 distinct points are needed).
issues.POLYGON_SELF_INTERSECTION: The polygon boundary crosses itself (at {lon}, {lat}). Fix the order of the points.
issues.POLYGON_HOLE_OUTSIDE: A hole of the polygon lies outside its outer boundary. Fix the plot outline.
issues.LABEL_POINTS_REMOVED: Label points next to the polygon were removed; only the polygon is used.
issues.RING_ORIENTATION_FIXED: The direction of the polygon outline was fixed automatically.
issues.Z_COORDINATE_REMOVED: Altitude was removed because EUDR does not need it.
issues.POINT_OVER_4HA: The plot has {areaHa} ha. Plots larger than {maxHa} ha must be entered as a polygon.
issues.POINT_POLYGON_RECOMMENDED: The plot is entered as a point. This is allowed, but a polygon is recommended.
issues.POINT_AREA_MISSING: The point has no area. TRACES would assume {defaultHa} ha.
issues.OUTSIDE_COUNTRY: The plot is not in the selected country ({country}).
issues.COUNTRY_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE: We cannot check plot locations for {country} yet.
issues.DUPLICATE_PLOT: The plot is almost identical to an existing plot ({ids}).
issues.AREA_ZERO: The polygon has no area (all points lie on one line).
issues.NO_GEOMETRY: The plot has no geolocation. It can only be used for a simplified declaration, not for a due diligence statement.
issues.CRS_GUESSED: The file does not state its coordinate system. We assume {crs} (Slovenian D96/TM), but it could also be {alternatives} (old D48/GK, ~600 m apart). Please confirm the right system.
issues.CRS_UNKNOWN: The file's coordinate system is unknown. Export the file in WGS-84 (EPSG:4326) or D96/TM (EPSG:3794).
issues.PARSE_FAILED: The file or row could not be read.
issues.EXPORT_TOO_LARGE: The GeoJSON file is too large ({bytes} bytes, max {max}). Split the shipment or simplify the polygons.
issues.SUPPLIER_SUBMITTED: Added by the supplier through the portal – not reviewed yet.

termsSections.p: IZVOR is a tool that helps collect and organise data for due diligence under Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (EUDR). At the user's request it can submit the due diligence statement to the EU Information System through the official interface (TRACES); the user confirms the statement and is responsible for its content.
The user (operator or trader) is responsible for the accuracy of the data, the risk assessment and the due diligence statement. Checks in IZVOR are an aid, not legal advice.
Data is stored on servers in the EU. You can download an archive of all your data at any time. Keeping records for at least 5 years is your obligation.
A buyer link lets someone view selected shipments without signing in. You can revoke it at any time.
We may update these terms; we will tell you about material changes in the app.

privacySections.p: The data controller will be named when the service is launched. TODO: preveri.
Email and password for sign-in, data about your organization, plots (possibly names of forest owners), documents and shipments, and an audit trail of changes.
Providing the service (contract) and helping you meet your EUDR obligations (your legal obligation).
Supabase (database and storage, EU – Frankfurt) and Vercel (hosting). Satellite imagery is loaded by your browser directly from the map provider (Esri).
Access, rectification, portability (ZIP archive) and erasure (delete account in settings). You can complain to your data protection authority.

help.title: Getting started
help.intro: Five steps from a plot to the due diligence statement and the buyer package.

steps.p: Enter suppliers (forest owners, companies), customers and products with HS code and tree species in Master data.
Draw a plot on the satellite map or import a file (GeoJSON, KML, Shapefile, CSV, Excel). Plots over 4 ha must be polygons. Set the supplier and harvest period.
Link felling permits, decisions, delivery notes and certificates to plots. The app warns you when a document expires.
Choose the customer, products with quantities and plots (also on the map). The checklist shows what is missing; for standard- or high-risk countries record a risk assessment.

steps.h: Submit the statement and send the buyer package
steps.p: Download the GeoJSON, enter the data in TRACES, record the reference and verification numbers and send the buyer a link or the PDF with a QR code.

faq.a: A point (with the area) is enough for plots up to 4 ha. Plots over 4 ha must be entered as a polygon (outline).

faq.q: How many decimals do coordinates need?
faq.a: At least 6 decimal places in WGS-84 (e.g. 46.051234). The export always writes 6 decimals.

faq.q: My file uses a national coordinate system.
faq.a: If the file states its coordinate system (e.g. the .prj of a Shapefile), plots are converted to WGS-84 automatically (D96/TM, D48/GK, HTRS96/TM, MGI Balkans 6/7, UTM 33N/34N). For Slovenian files without it you choose D96/TM or D48/GK.

faq.q: Does IZVOR submit the statement for me?
faq.a: Yes, once you enter your TRACES web-service user in Settings. Mark the shipment as ready and click “Submit the statement to TRACES”; the reference and verification numbers are filled in automatically once the system assigns them (usually within an hour). Without it, you enter the data in TRACES manually.

faq.q: How does a supplier enter their own plots?
faq.a: In Master data → Suppliers, open the supplier and create a link. The supplier opens it on a phone without an account, marks plots on the map and uploads permits. You then review them with “Review now” on the Plots page.
Only the chosen shipment: your company, products, plot map, DDS numbers and optionally the list of documents. Supplier names are hidden by default.

faq.q: How long must I keep the data?
faq.a: At least 5 years. In Settings you can download the full archive (ZIP) for inspections at any time; the audit trail records every change.
